# PRD: Team Workspaces (v1)

## 1. Overview and problem

**Product:** B2B note-taking app. **Stage:** [GAP: product stage not provided]. **Document purpose:** Pre-read for engineering and design leads to decide whether to start v1 and what to scope first.

**Problem (one line):** Teams cannot work together in a shared space in the app.

**Current sharing behavior:** [GAP: how notes are shared today, and with whom, was not provided.] This matters because the migration question (Section 6) and several requirements depend on it.

**Proposal:** Add team workspaces: a shared space where invited members create and work on notes together, with two roles (admin and member).

## 2. Goals and success metric

**Goal:** Let a team set up a shared space and collaborate on notes within it.

**Target success metric (set by product owner):** 20% of paid accounts create a workspace within 60 days of launch.

- "Paid account" is defined as [ASSUMPTION: an account on any paid plan; definition to be confirmed].
- "Create a workspace" is counted as [ASSUMPTION: the workspace-creation event, regardless of whether members are invited].

**Supporting metrics (all Proposed, not commitments):**
- Proposed: Share of created workspaces with at least one invited member who accepts.
- Proposed: Share of created workspaces with at least one shared note.

## 3. Users and roles

**User types:** [GAP: user types and account structure (individual, team, organization) were not provided.] For this PRD, two workspace roles are used.

**Proposed, needs confirmation: permissions split**

| Capability | Admin | Member |
|---|---|---|
| Create a workspace (becomes its admin) | Yes | n/a |
| Invite members by email | Yes | No |
| Remove members | Yes | No |
| Change a member's role | Yes | No |
| Rename or delete the workspace | Yes | No |
| Create notes in the workspace | Yes | Yes |
| Edit notes in the workspace | Yes | Yes |
| Delete any note in the workspace | Yes | Own notes only |
| Leave the workspace | Yes (see Req. 4.4) | Yes |

[ASSUMPTION: members may edit all shared notes, not only their own. Needs confirmation.]

## 4. Scope

**In scope (v1)**
- Create a workspace.
- Invite members by email.
- Shared notes inside a workspace.
- Two roles only: admin and member.

**Out of scope (non-goals)**
- Billing changes.
- SSO.
- Guest access.

## 5. Requirements

**5.1 Create a workspace**
1. A user can create a workspace with a name.
2. The creator becomes the workspace's first admin.
3. [ASSUMPTION: any user on a paid account can create a workspace. Who is eligible is to be confirmed.]
4. A user can belong to more than one workspace. [ASSUMPTION; confirm.]

**5.2 Invite members by email**
1. An admin can invite a person by entering an email address.
2. The invitee receives an email with a link to accept.
3. An invite has a visible status (pending, accepted) to admins.
4. An admin can revoke a pending invite.
5. An invitee who has no account can accept by creating one. [ASSUMPTION; confirm.]
6. Invites cannot grant access outside the admin/member roles (no guest access in v1).

**5.3 Shared notes inside a workspace**
1. A note created in a workspace is visible to all workspace members.
2. All members can create and edit notes in the workspace, per the permissions table.
3. Each note shows which workspace it belongs to.
4. When a member is removed, they lose access to the workspace's notes immediately.
5. Behavior when two members edit the same note at once: [GAP: the expected concurrent-editing behavior has not been defined; design and engineering to propose.]

**5.4 Roles: admin and member**
1. Every workspace member has exactly one role: admin or member.
2. Roles are enforced per the permissions table in Section 3, once confirmed.
3. An admin can promote a member to admin and demote an admin to member.
4. A workspace must always have at least one admin. The last admin cannot leave or be demoted until another admin is assigned. [ASSUMPTION; confirm.]
5. No roles beyond admin and member exist in v1.

## 6. Open questions

**Q1. How do existing shared notes migrate into workspaces? (Kept open; not resolved here.)**

*Why it matters:*
- **Engineering:** The answer determines whether existing sharing data must be transformed, how ownership and access carry over, and what happens to existing links. Requirements 5.3 and 5.4 cannot be finalized until it is answered.
- **Design:** The answer determines whether users see a migration prompt, a one-time conversion flow, or no change, and how users who share notes today find and understand workspaces.

*Options (listed without a recommendation):*
- Existing shared notes are left as they are, and workspaces apply only to new notes.
- Users or admins choose which existing shared notes to move into a workspace.
- Existing shared notes are moved into workspaces automatically.

Dependency: [GAP: current sharing behavior must be documented before this can be decided.]

**Q2.** Who on a paid account is eligible to create a workspace? (See 5.1.3.)

**Q3.** What is the expected concurrent-editing behavior? (See 5.3.5.)

**Q4.** Can members edit and delete all notes, or only their own? (See Section 3.)

## 7. Evidence gaps and assumptions

**Evidence gaps** (what the team should gather before or during kickoff):
- [GAP] How many accounts currently share notes, and how many people share per account?
- [GAP] What customers say about collaboration today: requests, complaints, workarounds.
- [GAP] How current sharing works (who can share, with whom, via what mechanism).
- [GAP] Product stage and user types.
- [GAP] How many paid accounts exist, and what the 20% target means in absolute numbers.
- [GAP] Whether the 20% target is grounded in any baseline or comparable adoption data.
- [GAP] Typical team size per account, to inform member limits and invite flow design.

**Assumptions to confirm**
- [ASSUMPTION] "Paid account" definition (Section 2).
- [ASSUMPTION] Workspace creation counts as the success event, with or without invited members (Section 2).
- [ASSUMPTION] Members can edit all shared notes (Section 3).
- [ASSUMPTION] Any paid-account user can create a workspace (5.1.3).
- [ASSUMPTION] A user can belong to multiple workspaces (5.1.4).
- [ASSUMPTION] Invitees without accounts can sign up through the invite (5.2.5).
- [ASSUMPTION] A workspace must always keep at least one admin (5.4.4).

**Not addressed:** Timelines, staffing, and technical architecture are outside this document because no information was supplied.
